memory_candidates.content: In this repo's typst/ sync-check (scripts/typst-sync-check.sh Check 1), only literal backtick-quoted spans in .typ files are grepped against live Lean source; #leansrc(module, name) call arguments are plain strings, not backticks, so they are exempt from resolution checking. When writing formal-math prose that names Lean identifiers, prefer #leansrc tags for citations and reserve backticks for identifiers you've already confirmed resolve via `grep -rl --include=*.lean --exclude-dir=Boneyard -F "$name" FormalSystem/`.

Typst gotcha: writing a value."stringLiteral" inside math mode (e.g. S."frame") does NOT produce field-access dot notation -- it silently compiles as juxtaposed content (the value followed by literal text) since string literals in math are plain text, not identifiers. It looks like a typo for S.frame but produces no compile error, so it survives naive `typst compile` verification. Real field access in math mode needs the field name as a bare identifier (no quotes), or the reference should be moved out of math mode into backtick-quoted prose.

When a research report prescribes a section outline where a later-defined term is used in an earlier subsection's definition (e.g. 'Complex algebra' referencing 'Shift set' before Shift Sets is formally defined), the forward reference is intentional structuring, not a defect -- resolve it with a parenthetical '(below)' or a forward pointer to the specific later subsection, rather than reordering content against the report's explicit outline.
